newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close down on pre-holiday selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close down on pre-holiday selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished lower on Monday as pre-holiday selling continued ahead of Friday's Mid-Autumn Festival, and brokers expected the market to consolidate at current levels through the week.
The weighted index closed down 36.11 points or 0.56 percent at 6,453.98. Turnover was T$40.23 billion.
The absence of bullish news also foreced investors to stay on the sidelines, brokers said.
"There is simply no incentive, so people have decided to adopt a wait-and-see attitude," said Allen Huang of Baring Securities.
The mid-morning announcement of Taiwan's August unemployment rate, which hit a 10-year high at 3.19 percent, further undermined buying confidence, brokers said.
Trading volume is likely to shrink this week, they added.
But brokers said they did not expect the market to take a plunge. "The 6,400-point level should be the initial support for the time being," Huang said.
Selling pressure emerged in most sectors, but stocks that lagged a recent rally gains attracted minor bargain-hunting.
The day's most-active issue, International Bills Finance, rose T$1.7 or 6.64 percent to T$27.3.

Electronic shares saw profit-taking on their recent gains. Tatung Co fell T$1.0 or 1.59 percent to T$62 in active trade but computer giant Acer Inc outperformed other shares to rise 70 cents or 1.78 percent to T$40.1.

Uncertain domestic politics is another concern, brokers said. Vice-President and Premier Lien Chan's expected administration report on Tuesday could spark a new conflict in parliament, Norman Lee of Foremost Investment said.
"Chaotic politics will only hurt confidence," he said.
A 6,400-6,500 trading range was seen for Tuesday.
